pointers.sentence: It passes `editable=False`, so a model form leaves it out, and carries the flags of a relation to one object, `is_relation` and `many_to_one` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKey.__init__`).

Nor has it a `remote_field` or a `related_model`, and a relation to one object with no model at the other end is what `Options.fields` leaves out of its list (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.fields`).
`Model._check_fields` checks a model's local and many-to-many fields, not its private ones (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._check_fields`).

`ContentTypesConfig.ready` registers `check_generic_foreign_keys` instead, which finds each `GenericForeignKeyDescriptor` among a model class's own attributes and runs its field's `check` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/checks.py:check_generic_foreign_keys`).
The field's name is checked as any field's, then the two fields it names (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKey.check`):

`GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.__get__` begins by reading the content type's key from the row, the foreign key's attribute content_type_id on a note, and not the content type itself (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.__get__`).

`GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.fetch_one` asks `ContentType.get_object_for_this_type` for the row, on the instance's database and through the model's base manager; a row that is gone gives `None`, cached like an object (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.fetch_one`).

A note whose cached object no longer matches is not among them, and keeps its entry: in the run, among four notes read under `FETCH_PEERS`, Endeavour's note, its object id set to 2, still gave Endeavour with no query (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.fetch_many`).

`GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.__set__` sets both fields from the object it is given, the content type by `get_content_type` and the object id from the object's key, and caches the object; `None` sets both to `None` and caches `None` (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.__set__`).
Both must match, the comment says; as text, an object id kept in a text field meets an integer key (`django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py:GenericForeignKeyDescriptor.get_prefetch_querysets`).

`GenericPrefetch` holds a list, refuses a queryset made by `raw`, `values` or `values_list` as `Prefetch` does, and hands the list to `get_prefetch_querysets` at the last level of its lookup (`django/contrib/contenttypes/prefetch.py:GenericPrefetch`).

A filter, an exclude or an ordering through a generic key fails as the name is resolved: `Query.names_to_path` refuses a relation field without a related model, which its comment says "cannot generate reverse relations", so the message speaks of reverse querying even for a field of the note's own (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.names_to_path`):
